notes:
Seleucid Empire, group me-05-c. Fourteen pages were opened (A budget of 14), plus the Atropatene page for the 221/190 vassal events.

Cliopatria rows to correct (all in keyframe_review): the -318 shape is Seleucus as satrap under the Macedonian empire, not the Seleucid state (state starts 312, per the lead and infobox; Seleucus enters Babylon in April 311); the -301 shape keeps the Indus, Arachosian and Gedrosian land ceded in 303; the Kingdom of Armenia outline (879 of 881 cells) sits inside the Seleucid shape 210-189 and is a vassal; the -170 shape holds Egypt for 170-165 where Antiochus IV occupied it 170-168; the -164 shape cuts the east in one year (4,762 cells to the Parthian shape) although the pages date Media 148/7 and Babylonia 141; the -144..-127 shape drops Babylonia and Media too early and omits Antiochus VII's recovery 133-129; the -91 shape runs to 78 though Tigranes held Syria from 83 (no Cliopatria shape 77-67).

Disagreements between pages: Panium 200 (Seleucid Empire page) vs 198 (Antiochus III page; the Syrian Wars page gives Panium no year, re-read 2026-10-19); annexation by Rome 64 (Syria province page; used as the end year to match Cliopatria) vs 63 (Seleucid Empire infobox); the submission of Atropatene 221 (Atropatene page infobox map; the reviewer corrected an earlier 223, which is Antiochus III's accession) and after 221 (Antiochus III page); Demetrius II captured 138 (Mithridates I page) vs 139 (Seleucid Empire page); Molon's revolt collapse 221 (the Antiochus III page; the Seleucid Empire page gives no date).

Cliopatria relation not supported: '(Allegiance of Seleucid Empire to Roman Republic)' 203..189. The Roman-Seleucid war page dates the war 192-188 and the terms (indemnity of 15,000 talents, hostages, fleet limits) to 188; nothing in the pages calls the Seleucids a Roman vassal in 203-189. Not recorded as a vassal event; the Roman Republic dossier (eu-03) should decide whether the post-188 indemnity period counts.

Not mapped (page silent or no shape): Thrace 'established a footing in Thrace' in 196 (Antiochus III page; Cliopatria never holds Thrace); Antiochus IV's capture of Artaxias and reoccupation of Armenia (undated on the Antiochus IV and Seleucid Empire pages); Antiochus Hierax's Anatolian realm (Third Syrian War page: 'promptly declared independence', undated); the Persis Fratarakas (3rd century, undated); Elymais and Characene (Parthian vassals after 141); the loss of Cilicia and Coele-Syria in the civil wars after 129 (Seleucid Empire page silent); the real reason Cliopatria cuts 487 cells to Parthia in 110 and 29 to Judea in 126 (confidence-1 loss events).

Pages that did not load: Seleucid-Parthian wars (twice, with and without the encoded en dash) and War of the Brothers (Seleucid). Both would date the 238 secession of Parthia, the 245 secession of Bactria, Hierax's Anatolian realm and the 225 Pergamene gains; those events are confidence 1-2.

Rulers: omitted. A documented list exists (List of Seleucid rulers) but no page of that kind was opened inside the budget; the pages give only partial reigns (Seleucus I 305-281, Antiochus III 223-187, Antiochus IV 175-164, Demetrius I 162-150, Antiochus VII 138-129, Philip II 65-63).
